paragraphs.text: "Give me a bit of steel and I'll deliver it into the hearts of my enemies."
A single light unleashes a hail of cleansing.
"Bend with the storm, then reply in kind."
The strongest of the pride are measured not by the steel in their hands but by the steel in their souls.
Her instinct is as sharp as her blade.
As the nim storm across the plains, a lone priest stands in their path. At his silent gesture, the battle line breaks, and the tide turns.
The Auriok have fought the metal hordes for so long now that knowing how to cripple them has become an instinct.
Defending to the death isn't always enough.
Before religion or civilization, there was order.
For the first and last time, the horrific creature experienced terror.
Leonin raising ceremonies take place at the white sun's dawn, the rebirth of artifacts mirroring the birth of a new day.
"I have seen the end of times, a future in which all our kind are torn from this world." —Ushanti, leonin shaman
Theirs is a craft brought about by necessity, now raised to the level of art.
Those who survive the test bear a mark of power anyone can recognize.
"Your arrogance is my best weapon."
Stealing goblin weapons would be easier if the goblins were smart enough to let go.
A single lie unleashes a tide of disbelief.
It could be made to run silently, but its low hum reminds the Neurok that they are always watched.
"Someday, someone will best me. But it won't be today, and it won't be you."
As long as there are questions to be asked, the vedalken will ask them.
After the researcher's astonishing success, his assistants spent six hours finding a way to return the specimens safely to the ground.
"Why should I be bound by rules when I can see so far beyond them?"
Before labs or lectures, there was insight.
"Today's paperweight, tomorrow's leveler." —Bruenna, Neurok leader
"Secrets are meant to remain secret." —Memnarch
Memnarch shared a touch of his power with the vedalken in return for their service. It is a debt he intends to collect.
Art is unknown to the vedalken—for them, all creations must serve a purpose.
"The druids would be better off if they spent more time in the lab and less time watching trees grow." —Pontifex, elder researcher
"May you wake to find you were only ever a dream." —Mephidross curse
"The one who dies with the most toys is still dead." —Geth, keeper of the Vault
Bottom feeders sometimes rise to the top.
The swarm's million wings stir the foulest of breezes.
A single fear unleashes a torrent of nightmares.
Mephidross claims all life within it. What cannot be twisted is absorbed.
Even on a world of metal, there are those who thirst for blood.
Their pain is so great, they can't help but share it with others.
In Mephidross, refuse doesn't last long—it's all scavenged, reanimated, or consumed.
Scavengers are always the first to pay their respects.
It is one of the oldest nim, steeped so long in the Dross that it has lost all vestiges of humanity.
Before tyrants or torturers, there was evil.
The beetles feed not on the flesh of corpses but on the metal, grinding out the iron and steel to add to their own bulky shells.
There's no escaping an enemy that lives inside your head.
When leonin settlers abandon their homes to the nim, items of value are often left behind.
Every creature on Mirrodin is a lightning rod.
Because fighting is easier than figuring out what else to do.
"If only the living were so easily salvaged." —Memnarch
"Is it the stomping kind or the munching kind?" —Slobad, goblin tinkerer
A single misstep unleashes an avalanche of ruin.
The spell fell upon the crowd like a dragon, ancient and full of death.
"Now I'm thirsty." —Korva, Vulshok battlemaster
Always easily impressed, Durg was about to be blown away.
A Vulshok weapon strikes with the fire of the forge that made it.
Fallen enemies are fed to the scavengers. Fallen friends are thrown into the Great Furnace, their souls returned to the Great Mother.
Before wars or weapons, there was anger.
"You might want to work on your aim."
"I used to joke that he had been exiled for being too smart. Now I know why he never laughed." —Glissa Sunseeker
Compared to the fire of the forge, the strength of steel is nothing.
It must eat its weight in metal daily, or its furnacelike belly will consume itself for lack of fuel.
Tel-Jilad's sworn protectors are the trolls, yet more fearsome protectors were created by the Tangle itself.
A single seed unleashes a flurry of growth.
In the Tangle, bad is often followed by worse.
Gelfruit grows abundantly wherever Sylvok druids live, as if the Tangle knows that humans are not as hardy as the beasts or as nimble as the elves.
"Ashes to ashes, rust to rust." —Viridian shaman
Before predators or prey, there was life.
From the Radix at the hub of the Tangle all the way out to the Edges of Forgetting, a Viridian elf's life is built around the temporary.
Wurms compete for nesting grounds near the Radix. The young who hatch closest have the best chance for survival.
Strange times make for strange allies.
They're considered good luck by the elves they don't eat.
In bringing life to Mirrodin, Memnarch was more successful than he knew—for Mirrodin began to take on a life of its own.
"When the levelers come again, we shall be ready for them."
Thanks to the wolves, Tel-Jilad is the one area of Mirrodin the myr don't see often.
"We have no sun to guide our dead, so I tend the prismatic flames of the spirit fires that show the souls their way. When I die, I hope there is one left to guide my spirit home."
"I will fight only the way nature intended—and nature intended us to win."
If taken, it cuts the hand that clutches it. If given, it heals the hand that holds it.
It breaches not physical distances but temporal ones.
Break in case of emergency.
The parts are as strong as the whole.
Everything in its path is either pushed aside or ground under.
It converts the faintest surges of power from Mirrodin's core into usable energy, providing endless power for Memnarch's creations on the surface.
"Did it have this shape upon Mirrodin's creation, or did some inconceivable force shape the unshapable?" —Pontifex, elder researcher
The ultimate treasure is one that guards itself.
Its curve mimics the twists of life and death.
Though no longer attached to the hand, it still holds its adversary in its grasp.
In close proximity, their magnetic energies merge and form a field of protection.
The longer it skulks through the corrosive gases of Mephidross, the more it adopts their thirst for death.
When Mirrodin's varied civilizations developed ways to fight the levelers, Memnarch upped the stakes.
"As the experimental population grows, so do the number of myr. It's a perfect equilibrium." —Memnarch
The book shrieks horribly until its cover is opened, granting the spirit inside a moment's rest from the painful stirrings of the book's contents.
The goblins built it far larger than the cave opening, but to their glee, it smashed into the mountainside, ripping itself a new exit.
Bright as a mirror, dark as the sea.
In the blur between metal and flesh, Memnarch found madness.
One thing the myr can't do is enjoy the scenery.
Memnarch created the myr with three qualities in mind: dependability, controllability, and disposability.
The longer it patrols the smoldering crags of the Oxidda Chain, the more it adopts their fiery temper.
The longer it stands among the deadly blades of the Razor Fields, the more it adopts their harsh exterior.
It rolls with the punches.
The longer it soars above the shimmering swirls of the Quicksilver Sea, the more it adopts their unpredictability.
The longer it weaves through the twisted vines of the Tangle, the more it adopts their hidden strength.
It still stares accusingly at Memnarch, though millennia have passed since he separated the eye from its body.
The undead may outlast the living, but those who have never lived outlast them both.
It gives legs to the earth and wings to the sky.
Some say the knowledge lost during the Ritual of Rebuking is returned through the well's waters.
"The lifespan of a wirefly can be precisely described as 'short.'" —Bruenna, Neurok leader
A wurm knows nothing of deception. If it opens its mouth, it plans to eat you.
Panopticon, forge of the Darksteel Eye, home of Mirrodin's keeper.
